Insurance Ombudsman India 2026: How to File a Complaint and Win

By Hari Kotian | Published on 2026-07-25

The Insurance Ombudsman is a free, quasi-judicial forum for resolving policyholders' disputes with insurance companies. If you have exhausted all internal grievance channels and still received no satisfaction, the Ombudsman is your next powerful step.

Eligibility: When Can You Approach the Ombudsman?

You can file a complaint with the Insurance Ombudsman if:

  • The dispute value is up to Rs. 30 lakhs (for 2024-26 cycle).
  • The grievance has been already been raised with the insurer and 30 days have passed without a satisfactory resolution.
  • The complaint is not being heard in any other forum or court.

How to File an Ombudsman Complaint

  1. Step 1: Write a complaint letter — Clearly state the facts, the amount claimed, the rejection reason, and the relief sought.
  2. Step 2: Attach all supporting documents — Policy document, rejection letter, grievance reference number, all correspondence with the insurer.
  3. Step 3: Submit online or offline — File via the IOB portal (https://www.cioins.co.in/complaint) or submit physically at the nearest Ombudsman office.
  4. Step 4: Await hearing notice — The Ombudsman will schedule a hearing within 15 days and issue a decision within 30 days.
  5. Step 5: Receive decision — The Ombudsman's decision is binding on the insurance company but not on you — you can still approach a court if unsatisfied.
